newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Retevision okays valuation for flotation.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Retevision okays valuation for flotation.

text.p: Spanish telecommunications group Retevision said on Tuesday it had approved a valuation for the firm ahead of its upcoming privatisation.
This is a decisive factor in fixing the share price for the initial public offering, due in principle next year.
At September 30 1996, the firm's net worth was 64.07 billion pesetas, with current assets of 11.43 billion pesetas.
At the same date Retevision had assets of 81.20 billion pesetas, of which fixed assets totalled 75.39 billion and financial investments totalled 5.81 billion pesetas.

Retevision posted net profit for the first nine months to September of 2.18 billion pesetas, up 24.7 percent over the year-earlier period, while operating income rose 12.2 percent to 27.31 billion pesetas.

The Spanish government is expected to approve a privatisation framework for the fully state-owned company in the coming weeks, after which the sale would take place up to around three months afterwards.
Retevision, Spain's second telecommunications operator after Telefonica de Espana, is due to be fully privatised by 2000, with many domestic and foreign groups said to be interested.
